362277.title: Bang-Jensen and Gutin's longest path algorithm conjecture for semicomplete digraphs
362277.statement: Let $D$ be a semicomplete digraph, and let $x,y$ be distinct vertices of $D$. A longest $(x,y)$-path is an $(x,y)$-path containing the maximum possible number of arcs. **Longest path algorithm conjecture.** There exists a polynomial algorithm for finding a longest $(x,y)$-path when the input is a semicomplete digraph $D$ and $x,y$ are distinct vertices of $D$. The complexity of finding such a path is stated to be open, even for semicomplete digraphs; the conjecture asks for a polynomial-time algorithm.
362277.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Yun Wang and Anders Yeo, “Generalized paths and cycles in semicomplete multipartite digraphs”, arXiv:2403.07597 (2024).
362277.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07597

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362314.title: Polynomial-time Hermite normal form conjecture for pseudo-matrices over $A_{fi}$
362314.statement: Let $A_{fi}$ be the function-field ring considered in the paper, and let a pseudo-matrix over $A_{fi}$ represent a module by its coefficient ideals and matrix. **Polynomial-time Hermite normal form conjecture.** There exists a polynomial-time algorithm to compute the Hermite normal form of a pseudo-matrix over $A_{fi}$. The analogous polynomial-time result is known for maximal orders in number fields, but the corresponding result for maximal orders in function fields is not known in the literature; the paper leaves its investigation to further work.
362314.source_name: Mickaël Montessinos, “Algebraic algorithms for vector bundles over curves”, arXiv:2403.09449 (2024).
362314.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09449

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362322.title: Unique-largest-antichain conjecture for balls in the Boolean lattice
362322.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\dots,p\}\cup\{p+1,\dots,p+q\}$ with $q=n-p$. For $i,j\geq 0$, let $X_{i,j}$ be the family of sets obtained from $[p]$ by subtracting $i$ elements and adding $j$ elements from $\{p+1,\dots,p+q\}$. Define the ball of radius $r$ centered at $[p]$ by

$$
B_r[p,q]=\bigcup_{i+j\leq r}X_{i,j}.
$$

**Unique-largest-antichain conjecture.** The largest layer of $B_r[p,q]$ is its unique largest antichain.

This concerns the width of a structured subposet of the Boolean lattice. The surrounding discussion presents determining or bounding the width of such subposets as a wide-open problem; the supplied text gives no resolution of this claim.
362322.source_name: Kada Williams, “The Width of a Ball in a Hypercube”, arXiv:2403.09943 (2024).
362322.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09943

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362338.title: Common minimum in- and out-degree conjecture for cycle orientations
362338.statement: Let $t$ be a positive integer. An orientation of the cycle on $t$ vertices is obtained by assigning a direction to each edge of that cycle. **Common degree conjecture.** Every digraph with minimum out-degree and minimum in-degree at least $t-1$ contains every orientation of the cycle on $t$ vertices as a subdivision. This is proposed as a common strengthening of known results for dichromatic number and polynomial minimum-out-degree bounds; its status is not resolved in the source.
362338.source_name: Chun-Hung Liu and Youngho Yoo, “Tight minimum degree conditions for apex-outerplanar minors and subdivisions in graphs and digraphs”, arXiv:2403.11470 (2026).
362338.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11470

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024). “The following conjecture of Mader from 1985 remains open.”

362339.title: Randomly shifted Gumbel convergence conjecture for the maximum of Ginzburg–Landau fields
362339.statement:
Let $Q_N$ be the domain, let $\boldsymbol{P}^{Q_N,0}$ denote the law in the notation of Theorem 1.1, and let $\boldsymbol{g}$ and $m_N$ be the corresponding constants and centering term. Set

$$
c^* = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\boldsymbol{g}}}.
$$

**Randomly shifted Gumbel convergence conjecture.** There exists a random variable $Z>0$ such that

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\boldsymbol{P}^{Q_N,0}\left(\max_{x\in Q_N}\phi(x)-\sqrt{\boldsymbol{g}}m_N\leq t\right)=\mathbb{E}\left(\exp\left(-Z\exp(-c^*t)\right)\right),\qquad \forall t\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

Theorem 1.1 establishes the tightness of the centered maximum, and this conjecture predicts the stronger convergence in distribution to a randomly shifted Gumbel law. The existence and identification of the limiting random shift remain open.
362339.source_name: Florian Schweiger, Wei Wu and Ofer Zeitouni, “Tightness of the maximum of Ginzburg-Landau fields”, arXiv:2403.11500 (2024).
362339.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11500

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362369.title: Three-colour random bipartite tree-cover threshold conjecture
362369.statement:
Let $G\sim G(n,n,p)$ be a random bipartite graph with two parts of size $n$, and let $\operatorname{tc}_3(G)$ be the minimum number of monochromatic trees whose vertices cover $G$ in every 3-edge-colouring. **Three-colour random bipartite conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ such that if 
$$
p\ge C(\log n/n)^{1/4},
$$
 then with high probability 
$$
\operatorname{tc}_3(G)\le 5.
$$
 This is proposed as the three-colour analogue of the two-colour threshold question and remains open.
362369.source_name: Camila Fernández, Matías Pavez-Signé and Maya Stein, “Monochromatic partitions in 2-edge-coloured bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2403.12587 (2024).
362369.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2204.00496](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.00496), [arXiv:1607.03348](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03348).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12587

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362381.title: Weighted-graph reformulation of the extremal partition conjecture
362381.statement:
Fix integers $s$ and $t$ with $3\leq s\leq t-2$. A weighted graph **admitting a $(b,t-1-b)$-partition** has $b$ vertices and $t-1-b$ parts satisfying the defining partition conditions for the weighted-graph reduction. **Weighted-graph reformulation.** The maximum $K_s$-density among weighted graphs admitting a $(b,t-1-b)$-partition is attained when

$$
b=\max\{s,\lfloor t/2\rfloor\}.
$$
 This is the weighted-graph form of the proposed extremal periodicity principle; the supplied text explains that the paper proves both conditions under which it holds and counterexamples, while no complete resolution is stated here.
362381.source_name: Jun Gao, Suyun Jiang, Hong Liu and Maya Sankar, “Generalized Ramsey–Turán density for cliques”, arXiv:2403.12919 (2024).
362381.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12919

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362384.title: The identification number bound for connected identifiable graphs
362384.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected identifiable graph of order $n\ge 2$ and maximum degree $\Delta\ge 2$. Write $\gamma^{{\rm ID}}(G)$ for the minimum size of an identifying code of $G$. **Identification number bound.** There exists a constant $c$ such that

$$
\gamma^{{\rm ID}}(G) \le \left( \frac{\Delta - 1}{\Delta} \right) n + c.
$$

This conjecture asks for the largest possible identification number of a connected identifiable graph in terms of its order and maximum degree. Earlier bounds showed that the identification number can be improved below $n$ by an amount depending on the maximum degree; the conjecture proposes the asymptotically sharp linear bound with an additive constant.
362384.source_name: Dipayan Chakraborty, Florent Foucaud, Michael A. Henning and Tuomo Lehtilä, “Identifying codes in graphs of given maximum degree: Characterizing trees”, arXiv:2403.13172 (2025).
362384.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13172

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362392.title: Triangle-free graph criterion for discontinuity in lower-tail probabilities
362392.statement:
Let $H$ be a fixed graph, let $p\in(0,1)$ be constant, and set

$$
m=p\binom{n}{2}.
$$

Let $G_m\sim G(n,m)$, let $N_H(G_m)$ denote the number of copies of $H$ in $G_m$, and write

$$
\mu_H=\mathbb{E}\left[N_H(G_m)\right].
$$

**Triangle-free graph discontinuity conjecture.** The function

$$
\beta\mapsto\frac{\log\log\mathbb{P}\left(N_H(G_m)<(1-n^\beta)\mu_H\right)^{-1}}{\log n}
$$

has a jump discontinuity at $\beta=-1$ if and only if $H$ is triangle-free.

This conjecture proposes a general criterion for whether lower-tail moderate deviations exhibit a discontinuity near $\delta=n^{-1}$. The paper describes the problem as wide open beyond the triangle case and relates the bipartite-graph behavior to Siderenko's conjecture.
362392.source_name: José Alvarado, Gabriel Dias and Simon Griffiths, “Moderate Deviations of Triangle Counts in the Erdős-Rényi Random Graph G(n,m): The Lower Tail”, arXiv:2403.13792 (2025).
362392.references:
**8 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2109.02906](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.02906), [arXiv:2108.06359](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.06359), [arXiv:2009.05428](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05428), [arXiv:2006.05511](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.05511), [arXiv:1801.06887](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06887), [arXiv:1708.08439](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08439), [arXiv:1601.05762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.05762).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13792

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362397.title: The finite axiomatizability conjecture for the pointed Weihrauch lattice
362397.statement: Let $\mathfrak{W}_\bullet$ be the pointed Weihrauch lattice equipped with meet $\sqcap$, product $\times$, and unit $1$, and let the paper's partial axiomatization be given by the axioms in Figure 1. **Pointed Weihrauch axiomatization conjecture.** $(\mathfrak{W}_\bullet,\sqcap,\times,1)$ is fully axiomatized by the axioms in Figure 1. The paper states this as a conjectural counterpart to the preceding non-finite axiomatizability claim, because the authors were unable to find a valid inequality in the pointed structure outside the stated axioms; its resolution is not given.
362397.source_name: Eike Neumann, Arno Pauly and Cécilia Pradic, “The equational theory of the Weihrauch lattice with multiplication”, arXiv:2403.13975 (2024).
362397.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13975

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362436.title: Maximum diameter of redundant non-surrounded graphs
362436.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ in which every vertex is redundant and no vertex is surrounded. Its diameter is the graph distance between vertices at maximum distance.

**Maximum-diameter conjecture.** The maximum diameter of such a graph is

$$
\left\lfloor \log_2(n)\right\rfloor;
$$

when $n$ is a power of $2$, this maximum is attained only by the $k$-cube and by graphs containing the $k$-cube as a subgraph.

The $k$-cube is given in the surrounding text as an example with $2^k$ vertices, diameter $k$, all vertices redundant, and no surrounded vertices. The supplied text does not establish the asserted upper bound or the uniqueness claim.
362436.source_name: Andrew Steane, “Distance-critical and distance-redundant graphs”, arXiv:2403.16197 (2024).
362436.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1709.03974](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.03974).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16197

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362440.title: Brinkmann, Preissmann and Sasaki's large-girth Type 2 conjecture
362440.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, meaning that every vertex has degree $3$, and let its girth be the length of its shortest cycle. A cubic graph is **Type 2** when its total chromatic number is $5$, namely, $5$ colors are required, equal to its maximum degree plus two. **Brinkmann, Preissmann and Sasaki's conjecture.** There is no Type 2 cubic graph with girth at least $5$.

The conjecture arose from the unsuccessful search for Type 2 snarks of girth at least $5$; it separates the large-girth and snark requirements. No resolution is reported in the source.
362440.source_name: Mariana da Cruz, Diane Castonguay, Celina de Figueiredo and Diana Sasaki, “An infinite family of Type 1 fullerene nanodiscs”, arXiv:2403.16310 (2024).
362440.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16310

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362467.title: Matching-size conjecture for random geometric graphs
362467.statement:
Let $X_1,\dots,X_n\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal{P}_n$, where $r$ and $d$ may scale with $n$, and let $G(\{X_1,\dots,X_n\},r,d,\|\cdot\|)$ be the corresponding geometric graph. Let $M_r$ be its largest matching, and suppose

$$
\mathbb{E}\left[|E(G(n,r,d,\|\cdot\|))|\right]=\binom{n}{2}\mathbb{P}\left(\|X_1-X_2\|_2^2<r^2\right)\underset{n\to\infty}{\longrightarrow}+\infty.
$$

**Matching-size conjecture.** Under this assumption,

$$
\mathbb{E}[|M_r|]=\Theta\left(\mathbb{E}[|E(G(n,r,d,\|\cdot\|))|]\wedge n\right),
$$

and the same order holds with high probability for $|M_r|$. This would give the typical largest-matching size from the expected edge count, capped at the number of vertices, in a regime where the expected number of edges diverges.
362467.source_name: Lucas da Rocha Schwengber and Roberto Imbuzeiro Oliveira, “Geometric planted matchings beyond the Gaussian model”, arXiv:2403.17469 (2026).
362467.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17469

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024). “However showing sharp necessary conditions for perfect recovery by $\lss$ when $d = \omega(\log n)$ is still an open problem.”

362468.title: Akbari et al.'s Caro–Wei bound for induced linear forests
362468.statement:
All graphs are finite, simple, and undirected; for a graph $G$, let $V(G)$ be its vertex set and let $d(v)$ denote the degree of $v$. A **linear forest** is a forest in which every component is a path. If $G$ has minimum degree at least $2$, then **Akbari et al.'s conjecture.** $G$ has an induced linear forest with at least

$$
\sum_{v\in V(G)} \frac{2}{d(v)+1}
$$

vertices. This conjecture strengthens the $k=1$ case of the Alon–Kahn–Seymour bound, which guarantees an induced forest of this order but does not require its components to be paths. The conjecture is the motivating statement of the paper; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
362468.source_name: Gwenaël Joret and Robin Petit, “A Caro-Wei bound for induced linear forests in graphs”, arXiv:2403.17568 (2025).
362468.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17568

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362507.title: Sols and Sols' conjectural bound for sections of rank-two bundles
362507.statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth irreducible curve of genus $g$, and let $E$ be a rank-two vector bundle of degree $d$ on $C$. Let $-e$ be the minimum degree of a twist $E\otimes L^{-1}$ having sections, where $L$ ranges over line bundles on $C$; assume that $\mathbb{P}(E)$ is not $C\times\mathbb{P}^1$.

**Sols and Sols' conjecture.** If

$$
-e\leq d\leq 4g-4+e,
$$

then

$$
h^0(E)\leq \frac{d+e}{2}+1.
$$

The conjecture concerns sharp bounds for global sections of rank-two vector bundles over curves and is tied to invariants of the associated ruled surface. The source provides no evidence of a resolution.
362507.source_name: Simone Marchesi and Alicia Tocino, “Homemade Algebraic Geometry. Celebrating Enrique Arrondo's 60th birthday”, arXiv:2403.19064 (2024).
362507.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19064

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362525.title: Hajebi–Li–Spirkl conjecture for graphs without large induced matchings
362525.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $h(G)$ be the smallest size of a subset of $V(G)$ intersecting every maximum independent set, and let $\omega(G)$ denote its clique number. An **induced matching** of size $t$ consists of vertices $\{a_i,b_i\}_{i\in [t]}$ whose only edges among them are $a_ib_i$ for $i\in[t]$. **Hajebi–Li–Spirkl conjecture.** If $G$ has no induced matching of size $t$, then

$$
h(G)\leq \omega(G)^{O_t(1)}.
$$

This conjecture asks for a polynomial bound on the size of a set piercing every maximum independent set in graphs excluding a fixed induced matching; the paper proves the stronger bound $h(G)\leq \omega(G)^{3t-3+o(1)}$, thereby resolving it.
362525.source_name: Jiangdong Ai, Hong Liu, Zixiang Xu and Qiang Zhou, “Piercing independent sets in graphs without large induced matching”, arXiv:2403.19737 (2024).
362525.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19737

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

362534.title: Center-realization conjecture for 2-Morita equivalent condensable algebras
362534.statement:
Let $\CC$ be a modular tensor category, let $(A_1,A_2)$ be a 2-Morita-equivalent pair of condensable algebras, and let $\phi:\CC_{A_1}^{loc}\simeq\CC_{A_2}^{loc}$ be the associated equivalence. Construct $B_\phi$ by choosing an indecomposable summand as described in the source, and let $\operatorname{Ext}_{A_i}(B_\phi)$ denote its extension over $A_i$.

**Center-realization conjecture.** An indecomposable subalgebra

$$
B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}_{A_1}(B_\phi)\ot\operatorname{Ext}_{A_2}(B_\phi)
$$

is the 1d condensable algebra corresponding to $(A_1,A_2)$, in the sense that

$$
Z_l(B)\cong A_1,\qquad Z_r(B)\cong A_2.
$$

This would establish the converse direction needed to recover 1d condensable algebras from 2-Morita-equivalent pairs. The source gives no proof or resolution.
362534.source_name: Rongge Xu and Holiverse Yang, “2-Morita Equivalent Condensable Algebras and Domain Walls in 2+1D Topological Orders”, arXiv:2403.19779 (2025).
362534.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19779

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362542.title: Pandigital and penholodigital prime digit-sum conjecture
362542.statement:
For a base-$b$ integer $n$, let $s_b(n)$ denote the sum of its base-$b$ digits. A **pandigital prime** (respectively, **penholodigital prime**) is a prime whose base-$b$ representation contains every digit $0,1,\ldots,b-1$ (respectively, every nonzero digit $1,\ldots,b-1$) at least once.

**Pandigital and penholodigital prime digit-sum conjecture.** For $b>3$, the smallest pandigital prime or penholodigital prime $n$ satisfies $s_b(n)=b(b-1)/2+2$ if $b$ is of the form $4k+3$, and satisfies $s_b(n)=b(b-1)/2+1$ otherwise.

The preceding theorems establish corresponding lower bounds, with the stronger bound in bases of the form $4k+3$. Numerical experiments are cited as evidence, but the conjecture is not resolved in the supplied text.
362542.source_name: Chai Wah Wu, “Pandigital and penholodigital numbers”, arXiv:2403.20304 (2025).
362542.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.20304

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

362582.title: The arithmetic transfer conjecture for odd type $(r,0)$
362582.statement:
Let $r$ be odd with $0\leq r\leq n$, and let $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_n$ be the formal scheme defined by the Cartesian construction above, with arithmetic intersection number

$$
\left\langle {\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}},g{\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}}\right\rangle_{\mathcal{N}^{[r]}_{n}\times\mathcal{N}_{n+1}}.
$$

**Arithmetic transfer conjecture for odd type $(r,0)$.** There exists $\varphi'\in C_c^\infty(G')$ transferring to $(c_r^2\\,\mathbf{1}_{K_n^{[r]}\times K_{n+1}},0)$ such that, for every matched pair $\gamma\in G'(F_0)_{\mathrm{rs}}$ and $g\in G_{W_1}(F_0)_{\mathrm{rs}}$,

$$
\left\langle {\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}},g{\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}}\right\rangle_{\mathcal{N}^{[r]}_{n}\times\mathcal{N}_{n+1}}\log q=-\frac12\operatorname{\partial Orb}(\gamma,\varphi').
$$

Moreover, every such transfer admits a correction function $\varphi'_{\mathrm{corr}}$ giving the corresponding identity with the additional term $-\operatorname{Orb}(\gamma,\varphi'_{\mathrm{corr}})$. This is open beyond the cases discussed in the paper; the density conjecture is stated to imply the correction-function formulation from the first part.
362582.source_name: Chao Li, Michael Rapoport and Wei Zhang, “Quasi-canonical AFL and Arithmetic Transfer conjectures at parahoric levels”, arXiv:2404.02214 (2026).
362582.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1503.06520](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.06520).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02214

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362612.title: Exact depth-three bound for two-colored random tournaments
362612.statement:
Let $f^*(2,3,n)$ denote the random variable measuring the largest number of vertices that can be reached from a vertex by monochromatic directed paths of depth at most $3$ in a two-edge coloring of a random $n$-vertex tournament. **Depth-three exactness conjecture.** With high probability,

$$
f^*(2,3,n)=n.
$$

This is the quantitative form of the preceding depth-three monochromatic domination conjecture: equality means that some vertex reaches every other vertex. It remains open in the source.
362612.source_name: Raphael Yuster, “Path-monochromatic bounded depth rooted trees in (random) tournaments”, arXiv:2404.03752 (2024).
362612.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03752

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362648.title: The monomer-dimer spectral independence conjecture
362648.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph, let $\lambda>0$, and let $\mu$ be the Gibbs distribution of the monomer-dimer model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda$. The quantity $\lambda_{\max}(\Psi_\mu)$ denotes the largest eigenvalue of its influence matrix. **The monomer-dimer spectral independence conjecture.** For any graph $G=(V,E)$ and any $\lambda>0$, the Gibbs distribution $\mu$ of the monomer-dimer model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda$ has $\lambda_{\max}(\Psi_\mu)=O_{\lambda}(1)$. The conjecture is motivated by the bounded spectral independence observed on regular trees despite their unbounded total influence; it is false for multigraphs with parallel edges, so the simple-graph refinement below is the unresolved form.
362648.source_name: Xiaoyu Chen, Xiongxin Yang, Yitong Yin and Xinyuan Zhang, “Spectral Independence Beyond Total Influence on Trees and Related Graphs”, arXiv:2404.04668 (2024).
362648.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362649.title: The simple-graph monomer-dimer spectral independence conjecture
362649.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple graph, let $\lambda>0$, and let $\mu$ be the Gibbs distribution of the monomer-dimer model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda$. The quantity $\lambda_{\max}(\Psi_\mu)$ denotes the largest eigenvalue of its influence matrix. **The simple-graph monomer-dimer spectral independence conjecture.** For any simple graph $G=(V,E)$ and any $\lambda>0$, the Gibbs distribution $\mu$ of the monomer-dimer model on $G$ with fugacity $\lambda$ has $\lambda_{\max}(\Psi_\mu)=O_{\lambda}(1)$. The large-girth theorem proves the claim for sufficiently large girth, while the parallel-edge example rules out the unrestricted multigraph version. The cases of simple graphs with intermediate girth remain unresolved.
362649.source_name: Xiaoyu Chen, Xiongxin Yang, Yitong Yin and Xinyuan Zhang, “Spectral Independence Beyond Total Influence on Trees and Related Graphs”, arXiv:2404.04668 (2024).
362649.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.04668

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362682.title: The ideal-adic semi-continuity conjecture for minimal log discrepancies
362682.statement:
Let $X$ be a klt variety, let $x \in X$ be a closed point, and let $\mathfrak{m}_x$ denote the maximal ideal corresponding to $x$. **Ideal-adic semi-continuity conjecture.** For every given $r \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, there exists $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ such that, for any ideal sheaves $\mathfrak{a}$ and $\mathfrak{b}$ on $X$ satisfying

$$
\mathfrak{a}+\mathfrak{m}_x^\ell=\mathfrak{b}+\mathfrak{m}_x^\ell,
$$

one has

$$
\operatorname{mld}_x(X,\mathfrak{a}^r)=\operatorname{mld}_x(X,\mathfrak{b}^r).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the minimal log discrepancy at $x$ is determined by a sufficiently high ideal-adic jet. The source attributes it to Mustață and Nakamura and presents it in a paper that gives a counterexample to a related conjectural property; the supplied text does not state that this conjecture itself is resolved.
362682.source_name: Yusuke Nakamura and Kohsuke Shibata, “A counterexample to the PIA conjecture for minimal log discrepancies”, arXiv:2404.06164 (2026).
362682.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06164

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362691.title: The eventual size bound conjecture for minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
362691.statement:
For each $k\geqslant 1$, let $N_k$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graph of order $n$ and size $|E|$. **Eventual size bound conjecture.** There exists an integer $N_k\leqslant 4k^2+2k$ such that every such graph on $N_k$ or more vertices satisfies

$$
|E|\leqslant \frac{(2k+1)(n-2k)}{2}.
$$

The authors note that they can construct small counterexamples and therefore impose the lower bound on the order; the conjecture's resolution is not supplied in the text provided.
362691.source_name: Amit Kumar Mallik, Ajit A. Diwan and Nishad Kothari, “Extremal minimal bipartite matching covered graphs”, arXiv:2404.06445 (2025).
362691.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06445

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362705.title: The minimum in-degree conjecture for small quasikernels
362705.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph. A **quasikernel** is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ such that every vertex is reachable from $Q$ by a directed path of length at most $2$. The minimum in-degree of $D$ is denoted by $\delta^-(D)$.

**Minimum in-degree quasikernel conjecture.** There exists an integer $\delta\ge 2$ such that every digraph $D$ with $\delta^-(D)\ge\delta$ contains a quasikernel $Q$ with

$$
|Q|\le\frac{1}{3}|V(D)|.
$$

This conjecture proposes that sufficiently large minimum in-degree forces a quasikernel substantially smaller than the general one-half bound. The source states that the behavior for general minimum in-degree remains unclear.
362705.source_name: Sam Spiro, “Generalized Quasikernels in Digraphs”, arXiv:2404.07305 (2024).
362705.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07305

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362792.title: Transversal Clifford impossibility conjecture for logical C-QSK circuits
362792.statement:
A stabilizer code encodes logical qubits, and a **transversal Clifford gate** is a physical Clifford operation that acts independently on the corresponding physical qubits. A **non-trivial exponentiated Pauli operator** is an exponentiated Pauli operator other than the identity case. The logical C-QSK circuit is the circuit under consideration for implementing such operators.

**Transversal Clifford impossibility conjecture.** There exists no stabilizer code where transversal Clifford gates realize the logical C-QSK circuit for any non-trivial exponentiated Pauli operator.

The preceding results rule out transversal Hadamard and transversal Phase implementations, and these gates generate the single-qubit Clifford group. The broader impossibility claim is presented as a conjecture and remains to be proved for arbitrary combinations of transversal Clifford gates.
362792.source_name: Zhuangzhuang Chen and Narayanan Rengaswamy, “Tailoring Fault-Tolerance to Quantum Algorithms”, arXiv:2404.11953 (2025).
362792.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11953

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362810.title: Harary–Hill conjecture for the crossing number of complete graphs
362810.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and define

$$
H(n):=\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

Here $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ denotes the minimum number of crossings in a plane drawing of a graph $G$. **Harary–Hill conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=H(n).
$$

The formula is achieved by Hill's drawing of $K_n$ and is conjectured to be optimal; determining the crossing number of complete graphs remains a central open problem in topological graph theory.
362810.source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Rosna Paul, Jenifer Viafara-Chanchi and Alexandra Weinberger, “On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs and layered graphs”, arXiv:2404.13155 (2025).
362810.references:
**5 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.07796](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.07796), [arXiv:1805.06780](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06780), [arXiv:1803.07515](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07515), [arXiv:1307.3297](https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.3297).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362811.title: Zarankiewicz's conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
362811.statement:
Let $K_{m,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $m$ and $n$, and define

$$
Z(m,n):=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{m-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

Here $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ denotes the minimum number of crossings in a plane drawing of a graph $G$. **Zarankiewicz conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_{m,n})=Z(m,n).
$$

Zarankiewicz constructed a drawing attaining this number, but a flaw was found in his claimed proof of optimality. The conjecture remains open in general.
362811.source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Rosna Paul, Jenifer Viafara-Chanchi and Alexandra Weinberger, “On the rectilinear crossing number of complete balanced multipartite graphs and layered graphs”, arXiv:2404.13155 (2025).
362811.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.13155

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362836.title: Faught–Nordhaus–Gaddum spectral-gap sum conjecture
362836.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement. Assume that both $G$ and $\overline{G}$ are connected; $\operatorname{Gap}(G)$ denotes the difference between the two largest eigenvalues of the transition probability matrix of the random walk on $G$. **Faught–Nordhaus–Gaddum sum conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Gap}(G)+\operatorname{Gap}(\overline{G}) \ge \frac{2}{\sqrt{n}}.
$$

This is a sum version of the Nordhaus–Gaddum problem for spectral gaps, under the connectivity hypotheses that make both gaps applicable. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
362836.source_name: Sooyeong Kim and Neal Madras, “A Nordhaus–Gaddum problem for the spectral gap of a graph”, arXiv:2404.15167 (2024).
362836.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362873.title: The edge-isoperimetric conjecture for the permutahedron at size $6^{(n+1)/3}$
362873.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Perm}(n)$ be the permutahedron graph, and let $i_k(G)$ denote the minimum edge-expansion among subsets of $G$ of size $k$. Set

$$
k=6^{\frac{n+1}{3}}.
$$

**Edge-isoperimetric conjecture for the permutahedron.**

$$
i_k\bigl(\operatorname{Perm}(n)\bigr)=\frac{n+1}{3}-1.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the heuristic construction using a Cartesian product of copies of the $6$-cycle gives the optimal edge expansion at this scale. The surrounding discussion does not provide a proof or a resolution.
362873.source_name: Maurício Collares, Joseph Doolittle and Joshua Erde, “The evolution of the permutahedron”, arXiv:2404.17260 (2026).
362873.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17260

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

362895.title: The maximum-filling formula conjecture for mixed even and odd board dimensions
362895.statement:
Let $\bar d(r,c)$ denote the maximum number of non-bonding dominoes that can be placed on an $r\times c$ rectangular board. **Maximum-filling conjecture.** If one of $r$ and $c$ is an odd multiple of $2$ and the other is odd, then

$$
\bar d(r,c)=\frac{rc}{4}+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

This is part of a proposed parity-based description of the maximum filling, inferred from the computed data and figures; its validity beyond the displayed cases remains open.
362895.source_name: Richard J. Mathar, “Bivariate Generating Functions Enumerating Non-Bonding Dominoes on Rectangular Boards”, arXiv:2404.18806 (2024).
362895.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18806

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

363029.title: The PSPACE-completeness conjecture for Trail Trap
363029.statement: Consider the decision problem ${\sc Trail Trap}\ {\rm P}{2}\text{-win}$: given a graph, determine whether the second player has a winning strategy in Trail Trap. **Trail Trap PSPACE-completeness conjecture.** The problem ${\sc Trail Trap}\ {\rm P}{2}\text{-win}$ is PSPACE-complete. The paper establishes NP-hardness on connected bipartite planar graphs of maximum degree $4$, but does not prove PSPACE-completeness; the conjectured stronger complexity classification remains open.
363029.source_name: Calum Buchanan, MacKenzie Carr, Alexander Clifton, Stephen G. Hartke, Vesna Iršič, Nicholas Sieger and Rebecca Whitman, “Trail Trap: a variant of Partizan Edge Geography”, arXiv:2405.05195 (2025).
363029.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363036.title: Kneser's conjecture on the chromatic number of the Kneser graph
363036.statement:
Let $[n]$ be a set with $n$ elements, let $k$ satisfy $n\geq 2k-1$, and let $\binom{[n]}{k}$ denote the family of all $k$-element subsets of $[n]$. A proper coloring assigns colors to the members of $\binom{[n]}{k}$ so that disjoint subsets receive different colors. **Kneser's conjecture.** The minimum number of colors needed for a proper coloring of elements in $\binom{[n]}{k}$ is

$$
n-2k+2.
$$

This is the chromatic-number statement for Kneser graphs, and it was proved by Lovász using the Borsuk–Ulam theorem; hence the conjecture is solved.
363036.source_name: Jingsi Hou, Guangyan Huang, Sammy Suliman and Haoran Yan, “Lovasz' Conjecture and Other Applications of Topological Methods in Discrete Mathematics”, arXiv:2405.05273 (2024).
363036.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05273

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

363067.title: Generic transitivity conjecture for primitive groups of finite Morley rank
363067.statement: Let $(G,X)$ be a connected primitive permutation group of finite Morley rank. **Generic transitivity conjecture.** Almost all such groups have maximum degree of generic transitivity at most $4$; the only exceptions are the groups listed in the rank bounds and classification conjecture. This is presented as a consequence suggested by comparison with finite primitive groups and Popov's theorem, but the meaning of “almost all” is not formally specified in the source.
363067.source_name: Ayşe Berkman and Alexandre Borovik, “Primitive permutation groups of finite Morley rank and affine type”, arXiv:2405.07307 (2024).
363067.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019–2024). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1909.02813](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.02813).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363117.title: Nonexistence of minimizers for sufficiently large charge
363117.statement:
Let $q>0$ be the charge parameter, and consider the minimization problem defined by equation (minmin1), whose minimizers are configurations attaining its minimum energy. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There exists a threshold $M>0$ such that for $q>M$ no minimizer occurs for the minimization problem.

The conjecture is motivated by the large-$q$ energy estimates developed in the paper and by the proof of Lu and Otto for the Thomas–Fermi–Dirac–von Weizsäcker energy. It asserts nonexistence of minimizers beyond a universal charge threshold; the supplied source does not indicate that this has been proved or disproved.
363117.source_name: Dario Mazzoleni, Cyrill B. Muratov and Berardo Ruffini, “An optimal design problem for a charge qubit”, arXiv:2405.10569 (2025).
363117.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.10569

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363168.title: The exact value of the normalized nine-point quadrilateral area
363168.statement:
Let $\Delta_4'(n)$ denote the minimum, over configurations of $n$ points in the normalized setting considered in the paper, of the area of a convex quadrilateral containing four points. The figure gives the lower bound $\Delta_4'(9)\geq 1/4$. **The nine-point quadrilateral conjecture.**

$$
\Delta_4'(9)=1/4.
$$

Equivalently, the other direction $\Delta_4'(9)\leq 1/4$ should hold. Establishing this would determine the exact value of the nine-point case, beyond the displayed lower bound.
363168.source_name: Rishikesh Gajjala and Jayanth Ravi, “Improved upper bounds for the Heilbronn's Problem for k-gons”, arXiv:2405.12945 (2024).
363168.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12945

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363258.title: Formal uncertainty principle implies duality
363258.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be theories, and let $\Delta A$ and $\Delta B$ denote their formal uncertainties. Suppose that $l>0$.

**Formal uncertainty–duality conjecture.** If $A$ and $B$ satisfy

$$
\Delta A\,\Delta B\geq l>0,
$$

then they correspond to dual theories.

This conjecture proposes that a formal uncertainty principle is sufficient for duality. The surrounding discussion emphasizes that the converse need not hold: dual theories can exhibit a formal uncertainty principle through deconstruction and reconstruction without necessarily satisfying a traditional uncertainty principle. The status of the proposed implication is not resolved in the supplied text.
363258.source_name: Renaud Gauthier, “Ground States of the -categorical Grothendieck Construction”, arXiv:2405.17135 (2024).
363258.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17135

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363284.title: The location-domination conjecture for twin-free graphs
363284.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices. A **twin-free graph** is one with no two distinct vertices having the same open neighborhood, and $LD(G)$ denotes its location-domination number.

**Location-domination conjecture.** If $G$ is a twin-free graph on $n$ vertices, then

$$
LD(G)\leq \frac{n}{2}.
$$

This conjecture, due to Garijo, González and Márquez, concerns the size of a smallest locating-dominating set in a twin-free graph. The source proves the weaker bound $LD(G)\leq \lceil\frac{5}{8}n\rceil$, improving the earlier bound $\lfloor\frac{2}{3}n\rfloor$, so the conjectured bound remains open in the supplied source.
363284.source_name: Nicolas Bousquet, Quentin Chuet, Victor Falgas-Ravry, Amaury Jacques and Laure Morelle, “A note on locating-dominating sets in twin-free graphs”, arXiv:2405.18162 (2024).
363284.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363286.title: The induced even-cycle-free Bollobás-Erdős-Tuza conjecture
363286.statement:
Let $k\ge 3$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph containing no induced cycle $C_{2k}$. Let $\alpha(G)$ denote the independence number, and let $h(G)$ denote the minimum size of a vertex set meeting every maximum independent set.

**Induced even-cycle-free conjecture.** If $\alpha(G)=\Omega(n)$, then $h(G)=o(n)$.

This is a proposed extension of the Bollobás-Erdős-Tuza conjecture to graphs with no induced cycle of length $2k$. The paper identifies it as an interesting direction; no resolution is supplied.
363286.source_name: Xinbu Cheng and Zixiang Xu, “Bollobás-Erdős-Tuza conjecture for graphs with no induced K_s,t”, arXiv:2405.18264 (2024).
363286.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18264

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

363317.title: Bounded chromatic number for bounded-degree color classes with no lonely colors
363317.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph whose edges are colored, and suppose that the subgraph induced by every color has maximum degree $d$. Say that a color is **lonely on a cycle** if it appears exactly once on that cycle.

**No-lonely-color conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, whenever no color is lonely on any cycle of $G$, one has

$$
\chi(G)\leq f(d).
$$

This conjecture strengthens the no-lonely-color variant of the question discussed in the paper. The supplied status evidence says that the related existence question for graphs with a one popular color coloring remains open; the conjecture itself is therefore recorded as open.
363317.source_name: Ignacio García-Marco and Kolja Knauer, “Coloring minimal Cayley graphs”, arXiv:2405.19543 (2024).
363317.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.19543

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2024). “On the other hand, it also remains open if graphs with a one popular color coloring exist that satisfy Conjecture .”
